title: Gun of Memory
text: “Hidden skills do seem like something that could exist. There are combination skills too, after all.”
“Ren and Itsuki appear to have learned Lunatic Judgment without even realizing it, I say.”
“About that mystery skill Motoyasu can use—wasn’t that a move only we could use back when we’d gone haywire?”
“If you’ve learned it, that’s a skill that requires you to be self-aware that you’ve gone haywire, you know.”
“It literally means becoming lunatic!”

Ren and Itsuki were talking like it was a skill they absolutely never wanted to learn, but what exactly did that mean! It’s a flashy skill you pick up while having a grand old time with Fleon-chan or Black Thunder, indeed! Father surely wanted to learn it too, I say.
“So, Naofumi, how’s it feel?”
“Um, it’s a skill that launches a slash, and right as it lands you overlay it with a reverse-grip strike using Air Strike Bash.”
“That’s quite the acrobatics… wouldn’t a plain Cross Slash work just as well? There’s already a skill called Cross Break for that.”
“Saying that kind of defeats the whole point, doesn’t it?”
“Hmm… like this? Air Strike Slash, followed by… Second… Slash Cross!”
And with that, Ren fired off a slash at an approaching monster, then layered a skill on top of it to finish it off.
“…So it turned into a combo skill. Considering the power and cost, not bad, but landing it deliberately seems like a pain.”
“I’d say landing it in one shot is pretty impressive though?”
“That’s thanks to stat bonuses. My speed stat makes it easier to catch up to the flying slash, so it’s simpler than it looks.”
There was probably some degree of weapon assist involved too, I’d wager.
“It’s just like my Drive Mode, I say.”
“Don’t lump it in with that. Also, yours definitely operates differently. You’re definitely doing that without any assist.”
Well, admittedly there’s no official skill name for it, but it’s essentially a combo, indeed.
“Slash Cross… fire it with an X and you’d get Double Cross, wouldn’t you?”
“Kind of chuunibyou in a way? You just keep firing Cross Break back to back.”
“You really do love crosses, don’t you.”
“That chuunibyou emoji thing—you type it as ‘dagger,’ right? Ren must know that.”
“Don’t drag it in that direction! If we’re going there, Itsuki’s got some weird cross-shaped weapon or skill too, doesn’t he?”
“You mean the one called Cross Fire?”
“It’s not like I use it by choice…”
Ren appeared to be trying to recruit Itsuki into his little club, I say.
“Tower shields are cross-shaped a lot of the time too… well, that’s just how they are. Oh, and in games, there’s sometimes that mystery crossbow thing too.”
Do you have one, Itsuki? Father asked.
“I do have one, but it’s got quite a lot of quirks.”
Itsuki transformed his weapon into a bow with two mysterious overlapping bows.
“It doesn’t draw normally at all.”
“Does it even fly like a proper arrow when you aim it?”
“It’s closer to a slingshot, honestly. The idea seems to be double the draw force means double the power, but frankly it’s just a failed design.”
“What does that say about Itsuki, copying such a failed design?”

“Mine’s just a copy of a bow some historical figure kept stored in Faubrey’s treasure vault, so it’s nothing special. Besides, the sacred bow can actually function properly in this shape since it’s not drawn with a string.”
Itsuki calmly shot back at Ren’s jab. Well then, allow me to add my own jab.
“Lately Itsuki’s been all about guns, I say.”
“And here I thought you were Bow Hero.”
“Oh, be quiet. Sure, the bow has higher attack power and better rate of fire in some cases, but a gun only needs a trigger pull, so that’s just what I’ve been using lately.”

This was, in essence, the historical shift from bows to firearms. Thanks to being able to launch a lead ball with just one finger, brute strength became unnecessary, I say. But in this world, stats govern how much power you output. A poorly made gun is no better than a toy, indeed. And given the complexity and cost involved, guns that are more trouble than they’re worth simply don’t circulate much.
“Ludgar and Moira are extremely powerful weapons, though. Isn’t there, like, an ultimate gun or ultimate weapon out there somewhere?”
“Well, as a gamer that’s definitely something I wonder about. What’s the strongest weapon in this world that I could actually use? Do you know, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Customization potential is extremely high, so I’d say every weapon has its strengths and weaknesses, I say.”
Just then, a scene surfaced in my memory—Itsuki using some strange gun. Where and when was that, exactly? Let me think for a moment, I say.
“Come to think of it… I recall Itsuki using some kind of loop somewhere… ah, no, a gun that fires magic.”
“You mean a Magic Radiator? A gun where you load a magic-imbued weapon like a staff into a tank, draw up the mana, and fire it.”
No, it was a different gun entirely, I think? Where on earth was that?
『Here, like this, and then—prepare the bullet like so—』
『Using your old skills again, huh? Making weird weapons in an alchemy class.』
『Come on, it’s fine, it’s a demonstration! There, done. Composite Magic Bullet Gun: Elemental Bullet, plus a full set of ammunition.』
『…That looks like a weapon that could summon monsters or something.』
A voice that sounded like Father’s played back in my mind!
“Do you know a gun called Composite Magic Bullet Gun: Elemental Bullet?”
“What’s that? Going by the name, it sounds like a gun that fuses magic together and fires it.”
“I can’t quite remember the details, I say. But I do recall Father commenting that it looked like something that could summon monsters.”
“I think I’m starting to get an idea of what it looks like. But at that point, isn’t it less of a gun and more like a magic cannon?”
At my words, Ren puffed out his chest as though he’d just spotted an opening for victory.
“Itsuki, seems like you’ve got your hands on quite the oddball weapon yourself, huh?”
“I didn’t make it! Naofumi-san, please give me more specifics, or people are going to start thinking I’m part of your chuunibyou club. Explain properly.”

“Hmm… it’s a weapon that showed up in some anime. Basically a summoning device shaped like a gun, I think that’s the accurate way to put it. You combine bullets to summon a powerful creature that fights on your behalf.”
“That exists in some games too. Summoning mechanics.”

Ren seemed to grasp that concept well enough, and honestly, so did I. After all, the highest-tier attribute magic in the demon realm’s terrain worked by summoning something to trigger its effect. And the special effects were spectacular, I say!

“Maybe it’s a reproduction of that kind of thing? If you think about it that way, you could probably make a gun that summons monsters you’re taking care of, if you really wanted to. Like… summoning Gaelion-chan to breathe fire and take down the enemy for you.”
“The moment you bring up Gaelion, the whole thing loses all its dignity. It’s supposed to be this cool effect where a dragon gets summoned and unleashes a devastating attack.”
I agreed wholeheartedly. Summoning Rival of all things was comedy of the highest order, I say.
“Following that logic, Filolials should have summoning magic too, shouldn’t they?”
“Come to think of it, Father and Fiancée have summoned little Filolial-sama and Raph-species as familiars before, I say.”
How exactly does one learn that? I’d been looping all this time and still had no idea, I say. Ah—no, wait, I recall Fan Pig—no, someone named Glass—had some creature under her command.
“Seems like summoning exists in this world too.”
“Well, we ourselves were summoned in the first place, so of course it exists. Meaning, this is essentially a small-scale summoning device.”
“Guess that’s about right. Anyway, back to crosses—”
“Don’t go back to that. X or cross, whatever, just get back to Itsuki’s story.”
“Double Cross, if you’re not careful with the effect, might end up looking like the character for ‘rice.’”
“That would instantly make it look uncool. Ren-san, we should be careful about that.”
“I said get back to Itsuki’s story!”
Ren’s voice echoed uselessly.
“Father, there’s the rice character, sure, but wouldn’t it more likely resemble a certain hole in one’s backside?”
“Motoyasu-kun goes straight for it…”
“I was deliberately avoiding saying that, and you just went and said it, Motoyasu-san.”
“Motoyasu, want me to turn your one hole into two?!”
The sheer audacity, thinking Ren’s attack could turn my backside into more than one hole! And so, exchanging banter like this, we continued on our way.
